title: Tenant-tethered escrow and proportional burst allocator PRD
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers with reserved GPU pools want predictable minimum capacity while still safely allowing short-term overage (burst) that is proportionally charged and reversible. Current reserved pools either strictly deny bursts or allow uncontrolled preemption that harms latencies and higher-priority tenants. We need a design that provides a tenant-tethered escrow (temporary credit/loan of capacity), a proportional burst allocator, and circuit-breaker style fallback so application SLAs are preserved.
problem_statement: Reserved capacity must guarantee (1) minimum throughput during common load, (2) predictable, auditable burst behavior with cost attribution, and (3) graceful fallback if burst capacity is exhausted or preemption occurs. The control plane must expose policy primitives to configure escrow budgets, reclaim rules, and tenant-level priority decay.
goals: Define an escrow ledger per tenant that tracks earned credits, pending loans, and repayment windows
Implement a proportional burst allocator that apportions available spare capacity by weighted tenant priority and recent usage
Provide an operator-visible audit trail and console controls for escrow balance, manual reclaim, and emergency drain
Ship a rollout with conservative defaults that preserve P99 latency SLOs for reserved tenants
non_goals: Not building a full marketplace for trading credits between tenants
Not replacing existing long-term reservation contracts or billing primitives (this complements them)
Not supporting cross-region live migration in this phase
success_metrics: Reduce P99 tail latency violations during tenant bursts by >= 70% for reserved customers using escrow mode
<= 2% increase in average per-token cost for reserved tenants under steady-state (non-burst) workload
Operator-visible reductions in manual incident pages relating to wrongful evictions (target: 40% fewer pages)
Console adoption: 30% of active dedicated customers opt into escrow-with-burst within 3 months
requirements: Policy primitives: escrow_budget (tokens/hour or gpus-minutes), repayment_window_seconds, preempt_priority (0-100), overflow_behavior (queue|reject|fallback)
Control plane: create/read/update escrow records, expose current balance, outstanding_loans, and history for last 90 days
Runtime: fast path in scheduler to allocate burst tokens proportionally across tenants with O(log N) decision latency
Telemetry: per-tenant metrics (escrow_balance, loans_outstanding, reclaimed, preemptions), events exported to console and metrics backend
Billing: annotate token-level usage with escrow_flag and loan_id for downstream accounting
Safety: automatic circuit breaker that disables bursting for a tenant when repayment_window is violated or global pressure exceeds threshold
Console UX: a dedicated escrow panel with balance timeline, manual reclaim button, and 'simulate burst' tester for admins
APIs/SDK: REST endpoints for querying escrow state and toggling tenant policy (with RBAC checks)
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests cover escrow ledger arithmetic, loan issuance, repayment, and failure modes
Scheduler allocates burst capacity proportionally in a 50/30/20 weighted tenant scenario under a synthetic overage test and respects preempt_priority order
End-to-end test where a tenant with escrow enabled performs a sustained 3x traffic spike: P99 latency stays within SLO; loans are recorded; console shows loan history
Operator can perform a manual reclaim from console and the reclaim action reduces loaned capacity within 60s and logs an audit event
Billing pipeline receives escrow_flagged usage with loan_id and matches simulated invoice in a reconciliation job
Security review completed and RBAC gating prevents non-admins from toggling other tenants' escrow settings
rollout_plan: Phase A: internal dogfood with three pilot tenants on dedicated pools (2 weeks) -> Phase B: opt-in beta for 15 customers with monitoring & oncall posture (4 weeks) -> Phase C: gradual default enable for new reserved contracts with telemetry-backed safety gates (6 weeks). Rollback plan: disable escrow issuance and auto-sweep outstanding loans to read-only mode; fall back to existing strict-reserve deny policy.
monitoring_and_alerting: New alerts: EscrowLoanFailureRate > 0.5% over 5m, GlobalBurstSaturation > 80% for 2m, TenantRepaymentMiss > 1% for 24h. Dashboards: per-tenant escrow balance, global spare capacity, preemption counts. Traces link from console event -> scheduler decision -> runtime enforcement.
implementation_notes: Propose using existing capacity ledger schema but add loan_id references. Scheduler change is minimial in API surface but requires lock-free atomic compare-and-swap on per-pool credit counters. Prefer eventual consistency for console balances with authoritative source in control plane database. Consider a server-side simulator to tune proportional weights before rollout.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: runaway debt accumulation if repayment windows are too lax -> Mitigation: conservative default repayment_window (1 hour) and hard cap on concurrent loans
Risk: billing mismatch -> Mitigation: end-to-end reconciliation job and test harness before GA
Risk: preemption-induced cascading latency -> Mitigation: circuit-breaker and conservative burst allocation fraction (max 20% of spare capacity by default)
